description: The provided image displays three side-by-side bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, each illustrating the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model across different quantization bit settings (3, 4, 8, and 16 bits) for two methods: “Uniform” (blue bars) and “Ours” (orange bars). In each chart, the horizontal axis represents “Quantization Bits” and is labeled with the discrete values 3, 4, 8, and 16, while the vertical axis represents “Perplexity” with a linear scale. The y-axis ranges from 0 to a maximum value specific to each chart: 30 for (a) WikiText, 400 for (b) PTB, and 30 for (c) C4, with tick marks at regular intervals (e.g., every 5 for WikiText and C4, every 50 for PTB). Each chart contains two bars per quantization bit, grouped side-by-side, with the “Uniform” method consistently shown as the blue bar and “Ours” as the orange bar. In chart (a) WikiText, the perplexity for “Uniform” is approximately 30 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 27 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. The “Ours” method shows lower perplexity, approximately 22 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 19 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. In chart (b) PTB, the “Uniform” method shows a much higher perplexity, starting at approximately 400 at 3 bits and decreasing to around 300 at 4 bits, then 300 at 8 bits, and 300 at 16 bits. The “Ours” method shows significantly lower perplexity, approximately 250 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 180 at 4 bits, then 180 at 8 bits, and 180 at 16 bits. In chart (c) C4, the “Uniform” method starts at approximately 30 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 25 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. The “Ours” method shows lower perplexity, approximately 21 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 19 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. The bars are not sorted by value and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coding.
